title: Stream Batcher: Instrumentation, Heuristics, and Tail-Focused Experiments
content:
Purpose and quick summary:
This doc collects the instrumentation we added to the streaming/continuous batcher, the heuristics we prototyped (age-informed reclamation, slot-level leaky buckets), and a compact run-log of exploratory experiments aimed at reducing p99 tail without regressing throughput. The focus here is practical: lightweight counters, low-overhead traces, and reproducible micro-experiments.

Background / motivation:
- We keep seeing hard p99 spikes on small-batch workloads with mixed lengths: chat-like (few tokens) + long context completions. Automatic batching reduces cost but introduces long tails when a single long request blocks a slot or when small urgent requests starve.
- Previous notes focused on batch-formation and timeout sweeps; this doc centers on what we measure (so we can reason about tradeoffs) and two new heuristics we trialed that are different from earlier sweep-based approaches.

Instrumentation added (summary of counters / traces):
- counter.batch_formed_count (labels: model, pool_id, batch_size) -> increments every flush.
- histogram.batch_formation_delay_ms (labels: pool_id, model) -> time between first request in batch and flush.
- gauge.slot_occupied_ms (labels: slot_id, pool_id) -> accumulative occupancy time per slot (for detecting long-blockers).
- counter.reclaimed_requests (labels: reason=[age_reclaim, size_reclaim, preempt]) -> how often we forcibly move requests between queues.
- histogram.per_request_kvcache_latency_ms -> KV cache lookup time per request, correlates with long completion overheads.
- gauge.pending_priority_levels (labels: urgent, normal, background) -> snapshot of backlog composition.
- trace.span:batch_lifecycle (fields: batch_id, size, wait_ms, slots_involved, eviction_reason) -> lightweight span sampled 0.5% of batches.

Why these metrics: we wanted to separate (a) batch formation latency, (b) slot-level blocking behavior, and (c) reclamation/preemption events. Earlier runs lacked per-slot occupancy metrics which hid the effect of long-running single requests monopolizing a GPU slot.

New heuristics prototyped:
1) Age-Informed Micro-Reclamation (AIMR)
- idea: when a new urgent request exceeds an age threshold relative to the oldest queued request in a different slot, attempt to reclaim the oldest small request by moving it into an outgoing microbatch (bounded by a microbatch_size_limit).
- knobs: reclaim_age_ms (default 60ms), microbatch_size_limit (default 4), reclaim_rate_limit_per_slot (default 1/sec).
- expected win: reduce p99 for urgent requests with minimal extra small-batch overhead.
- risks: increased number of tiny batches -> throughput loss / kernel inefficiency.

2) Slot Leaky-Bucket (SLB) for long request smoothing
- idea: each GPU slot exposes a leaky-bucket token budget representing remaining patience. Long-running request consumes tokens proportional to expected token-per-step cost; when budget drops below a threshold, slot signals 'soft-drain' and is deprioritized for new batch formation for short requests.
- knobs: slot_budget_ms (default 120ms), drain_threshold_pct (default 0.25), deprioritize_duration_ms (default 150ms).
- expected win: avoids starvation of short urgent requests that otherwise queue behind a long request; better tail fairness across request-length cohorts.

Experiment matrix (what we ran):
- baseline: current prod behavior (timeout=50ms, max_batch=16, fairness=age-weighted default).
- AIMR sweep: reclaim_age_ms in [30, 60, 120], microbatch_size_limit in [2,4,8], rate_limit in [0.5/s, 1/s, 2/s]. Each cell run for 30m steady-state with synthetic mixed workload (60% short 2–10 tokens, 30% medium 50–200 tokens, 10% long 1k+ tokens).
- SLB sweep: slot_budget_ms in [60, 120, 240], deprioritize_duration_ms in [100, 150, 300], and drain_threshold_pct [0.1, 0.25, 0.5].
- Combined: AIMR + SLB with conservative knobs.
- Noise injection: intermittent microbursts (100 reqs within 50ms) and cold-KV-cache bursts to exercise interaction with KV cache.

Key measured signals (collected every 10s):
- p50/p95/p99 latency for urgent vs normal vs background routes.
- throughput (tokens/sec, requests/sec) by route.
- GPU utilization by slot (sampled 1s).
- small-batch overhead: extra bytes and ms per microbatch compared to steady 8-sample kernel.
- fairness score: ratio of p99(normal)/p99(urgent) and starvation_incidence (fraction of urgent requests > reclaim_age_ms).

Representative results (high-level):
- AIMR: reclaim_age_ms=60, microbatch_size_limit=4, rate_limit=1/s reduced urgent p99 by ~18% vs baseline with a throughput drop of ~2.5% (tokens/sec) on the mixed workload. Small-batch counts increased by +12%.
- AIMR with too-aggressive reclaim_age_ms=30 cut urgent p99 further but throughput hit grew to ~7% and GPU kernel inefficiency increased (measured by kernel-invocations/sec).
- SLB: slot_budget_ms=120 + deprioritize_duration_ms=150 reduced cross-cohort interference: urgent p99 down ~12% and medium p99 up ~3% (acceptable trade). GPU utilization variance decreased (fewer long-occupied slots).
- Combined conservative knobs matched most of AIMR p99 improvements but with smaller throughput regression (~1.5%).
- Under KV-cache cold bursts, AIMR caused slightly higher tail since reclaimed microbatches triggered KV cache misses; SLB combined with a slight KV cache prewarm heuristic mitigated this.

Observability notes / dashboards to build
- Live panel: batch formation rate, microbatch fraction, reclaim counter, p99 split by route.
- Per-pool heatmap: slot_occupied_ms percentile + pending_priority_levels.
- Traces: sample spans for batches where reclaim/reassign triggered, for quick root cause.

Open questions / TODOs
- Cost accounting: need token-level cost delta for microbatches -> estimate per-request cost regression to feed Optimize recommendations.
- Interaction with autoscaling: aggressive AIMR increases small-batch churn which can change autoscaler signals (CPU/GPU churn). Validate on Dedicated pools.
- Evaluate on real customer traffic (opt-in beta) for 48–72h to check behavioral drift.
- Formalize fairness metric (currently ad-hoc). Consider a normalized latency-SLO delta across cohorts.

Quick run log (notes-to-self style)
- 2025-11-04 09:10 – started AIMR basic prototype on dev cluster; instrumentation in PR-482 (see linked_artifacts).
- 2025-11-07 14:22 – added slot_occupied_ms gauge. Observed 6 slots where single request held slot >4500ms during typical 99th percentile events.
- 2025-11-10 11:03 – AIMR(60,4,1) 30m run: urgent p99 reduced but microbatch counts doubled in first 5m while KV cache warmed then stabilized.
- 2025-11-18 16:45 – SLB prototype yields smoother slot occupancy. Combined run on 2025-11-21 looked promising; saved 14% p99 with -1.6% throughput.
- 2025-12-02 10:12 – injected microburst noise, noticed reclaim storms when rate_limit unset (we added 1/s guard).

Risks and mitigations
- Risk: too many tiny batches -> kernel starvation + cost regression. Mitigate by microbatch_size_limit and reclaim_rate_limit. Add an offline kernel-simulator to estimate kernel CF (cache/compute) costs for proposed microbatch distributions.
- Risk: regressions on long-running batches (QoQ for long requests). Mitigate with SLB deprioritization windows and A/B rollout with canary traffic.
- Risk: observable blindspots. Mitigate by adding sampled spans for batches hitting reclaim/reassign flows and by a postmortem template when p99 increases >10%.

Next steps (action items)
- [Ava] finalize dashboard tiles and create a lightweight alert when reclaim_rate > 0.5% sustained for 10m.
- [Marcus] run scaled Dedicated pool test with AIMR conservative knobs for 48h (ticket ENG-1324).
- [Priya] add per-request cost delta estimate in telemetry and short PR to Optimize team.
- [Leo] run kernel-simulator on microbatch distributions observed in the wild and report expected kernel throughput delta.

Appendix: sample counter table (for onboarding)
- batch_formed_count: increment when batch is flushed; tag by size. Useful to compute microbatch_fraction = sum(batch_formed_count[size<=4]) / total.
- reclaim_rate = reclaimed_requests / batch_formed_count over window.
- slot_blockers = count(slot_occupied_ms > 2000ms) by pool.
- starvation_incidence = count(urgent_requests_wait_ms>reclaim_threshold) / urgent_total.

References / links in context:
- PR-482: AIMR prototype code + tests.
- Confluence: Batcher Telemetry Design (linked above).
- Slack: #serving-batching thread (search: "AIMR reclaim storms").

Unresolved: best formal fairness metric, exact cost delta we can attribute to microbatch churn, and expected behavior for extremely long-tail LLMs (10k+ tokens) where slot_token_consumption variance is huge.

Notes to self: prioritize low-risk rollout: conservative AIMR + SLB deprioritization, tightly rate-limited, run with tracing and daily checks. Stop if reclaim_rate > 1% sustained and p95 of normal route increases >5%.
